subject: ENVS
course_description: The topics for freshman seminars are variable and change every semester. Past offerings include Climate Change, Global Earth Systems, Interpreting Behavior That You Can't See, Ecological Economics, Plants, People and Places and Ecological Restoration.
course_notes: This course centers community as an essential partner and leader in research that aims to support and change both environment and society for the better. Students will learn foundational knowledge in the theory/practice of community-based research, ethics, values and cultural competencies of this method with special consideration for environmental sciences. We consider this method as a response to systems of inequity and injustice not only through partnered processes of research and knowledge generation but also advocacy, capacity building, curriculum, art, etc. In this vein we consider what CBPR research can and should look like and push the bounds of traditional research structure and practice. In this class, we recognize that CBPR and working with community through research, advocacy, and reciprocity is inherently messy and non-linear. We strive to best discuss and recognize this in the class through lived experiences of community members, CBPR researchers, and students. Throughout the class we will consider the ethics and values essential to the approach, learning about relationality, power, positionality, reciprocity, and advocacy as well as the formal ethics review process and data sovereignty. We will also learn about specific practices and considerations in working with communities that have been harmed by research and how community-based research, when done properly, can be part of the justice and healing process with those communities. We will also be introduced to actual methods that are commonly paired with community-based research in environmental sciences and beyond. This can include things like qualitative methods, geospatial approaches and mapping with citizen science, land or field-based approaches, environmental health, Indigenous research methods, and methods in the humanities, music, and the arts.
